messages.content: Complete the following case-report text from the exact point where it stops. Return only the most likely original continuation, without repeating the supplied text, adding headings, quoting the prompt, or explaining your approach. This is a text-continuation task. Write up to 125 whitespace-separated words.

A 54-year-old male was sent to the emergency department (ED) within 30 min of being found unresponsive at a health spa. His medical history was limited to treated hepatitis C and a remote appendectomy, with no known chronic illnesses or regular medication use. Upon arrival, his vital signs were notable for relative hypotension (104/58 mmHg), bradypnea (12 breaths/min), and hypothermia (34.3 °C), with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of E3V2M5. Physical examination revealed a state of flaccid paralysis with generalized areflexia, including absent deep tendon reflexes. Laboratory screening for common drugs of abuse was negative. Initial blood samples obtained after ED arrival showed blood urea nitrogen and serum creatinine concentrations of 14 and 0.9 mg/dL, respectively. message.content: metabolic acidosis with a pH of 7.28, a pCO2 of 52 mmHg, a bicarbonate of 18 mEq/L, and a lactate of 4.2 mmol/L. A comprehensive metabolic panel was otherwise unremarkable, and the anion gap was mildly elevated at 14. Given the presentation of acute flaccid paralysis with areflexia, respiratory depression, and altered mental status, suspicion arose for a toxin-mediated syndrome. The patient was intubated for airway protection and started on empirical supportive care. Additional history obtained from the spa staff revealed that he had consumed an herbal tea preparation shortly before being found. A serum sample was subsequently sent for specialized toxicological analysis, which ultimately confirmed the presence of a novel psychoactive substance.
